foil.title: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption state
foil.scenario_short: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption remains at 63% over 30 days, driven by a 72% state confirmation of disruption feeding energy supply shock with 56% pressure and 4 urgent critical signals.
foil.perspective_strategic: The 72% state confirmation of disruption and 4 urgent critical signals indicate a structurally embedded risk, but the absence of headline evidence suggests the market is pricing on model signals rather than observable events.
foil.perspective_contrarian: The lack of directly matched headlines and the 75% confidence level suggest the 63% probability may be resilient; however, if no new reporting appears, the system could stabilize as actors rebalance positions away from the current path.
foil.actor_lens: Commodity traders: Price whether stress in Red Sea becomes durable over the 30d. Rebalance positions if the probability path moves away from 63%.
foil.top_signal: Red Sea maritime disruption state is feeding energy repricing through energy supply shock, with 56% pressure and 72% state confirmation

seismic-infrastructure.absence_reason: No product publishes a seismic forecast — earthquakes are not predictable, so there is no forecast/intel alternative to azimuth's observed USGS record. This is the honest inverse: for an observed natural-hazard fact, the sourced record IS the only trustworthy source.
